A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Human Simulacra dataset, MACM framework and evaluation study. All ten pages of each, including figures, tables, limitations and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original self-report experiments in Table 2, human observer assessments in Table 3 and qualitative dialogue results in Figure 5.

after.justification: v5 retains the original quantitative experiments and human assessments in Tables 2–3 and qualitative results in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same character-generation procedure, personality-ranking scheme, memory construction and four-agent MACM process. Redrawn Figures 2–3 reorganize and relabel these components without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eleven fictional characters and retain the self-report, observer-report and Mary Jones dialogue scenarios. No dataset, population or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same None, Prompt, RAG and MACM comparisons across the same models. Table 3 and Figure 5 retain the same Prompt, RAG and MACM comparisons on GPT-4-Turbo.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 adds Llama-2-70b and Llama-2-70b-Chat to its prose model list, but both already appear in v1's Table 2. The tested configurations, question types, option shuffling and human-assessment procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 retains the same adversarial knowledge-boundary challenge and nature-exhibition invitation case study. Figure 5's added success/failure symbols redisplay existing judgments; no ablation or robustness analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report self-report averages over three repeated tests, qualitative examples selected from three tests and observer scores averaged across two judges per assessment task. Neither adds seeds, variability estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain all numerical entries, including GPT-4-Turbo MACM scores of 44.00 for self reports and 38.75 for observer reports. Figure 5 preserves the same prompts and responses, and the reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The information hierarchy and personality-ranking scheme are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and the revised diagrams introduce no new mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about character generation, MACM and psychology-guided evaluation. Replacing 'A Step toward' with 'Benchmarking' in the title does not substantively change those claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of model-capability dependence, RAG's limitations and MACM's behavior. The limitations concerning synthetic-data depth, subjective human evaluation, knowledge boundaries and adversarial vulnerability are unchanged.

D1.justification: Generation parameters, profile counts, iteration budget, memory-construction details and the future code/data release statement are unchanged. The expanded model list in Section 6.1 repeats information already disclosed in v1's Table 2.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning remain the same. 'Hutson and Mastin, 2023' becomes 'Hutson, 2023', but the reference remains the same Guinea pigbots article; this is a bibliographic attribution edit.

P1.justification: The title and author/affiliation block change, Section 6.1 expands its model enumeration, and the Hutson citation attribution is edited. The section order, narrative and nearly all body prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially reorganized into workflow columns and separate subprocess panels. Figure 3 is redrawn with consistent agent colors, new icons and typography. Figure 5 adds shaded headers and success/failure markers. These substantially revise the central illustrations while retaining their underlying content; tables remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The separated workflow panels in Figure 2 and consistent agent colors in Figure 3 make the framework easier to follow, while Figure 5 makes existing judgments more explicit. Section 6.1 also better matches the reported model list. These provide limited clarity and consistency gains; the scientific evidence and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
